_comment: Single source of truth for the third-party libraries vendored under
both re-derives each version from the shipped files (drift) and queries
OSV for advisories affecting the pinned version (audit).
'probe' locates the version inside the vendored tree: 'file' is relative
to the library directory and 'pattern' is a Python regex in which the
token {version} is replaced by the escaped 'version' value.
'npm' is the registry coordinate used for the OSV lookup; omit it for
libraries with no upstream package (fork-local or internal ones) and set

Chart.notes: Minified with no banner; the only version anchor is a bare assignment, so the probe is deliberately loose. Bundles @kurkle/color 0.3.2. Lazily loaded via @web/core/lib/chartjs.

ace.notes: src-noconflict build variant. mode-qweb.js is fork-local, not upstream: it subclasses XmlHighlightRules and reads $rules.attributes[0].regex, so re-check it against mode-xml.js on every bump. Lazily loaded as the web.ace_lib bundle.

bootstrap.notes: JS bundle plus the full scss/ tree, which the design system compiles against. Popper is its only reason to exist here.

diff_match_patch.notes: Trimmed fork carrying the diff functions only; see the header comment for the modifications. No upstream version to track.

dompurify.notes: Upstream dist/purify.es.mjs, verbatim. Security-critical: it backs html_editor's sanitize plugin, which passes ADD_TAGS/ADD_ATTR — the exact config surface several past advisories targeted. Treat any advisory here as release-blocking.

fullcalendar.notes: Upstream all/global.js carrying 7 AgroMarin: markers, the last of which is a hand-written ESM export footer. skeleton.css MUST be replaced in the same commit: v7 regenerates its fc-* class hashes on every build and recycles some onto unrelated roles. Resolve those names through fcInternalClassName(), never by literal.

hoot.notes: Odoo HOOT test framework; developed in-tree and versioned with the fork.

hoot-dom.notes: Odoo HOOT DOM helpers; developed in-tree and versioned with the fork.

joint.notes: NOT a pristine upstream file. @joint/core ships no single-file ESM -- its joint.mjs is a 97-byte re-export shim over ~250 modules under src/, and dist/joint.js is UMD -- so build.sh bundles entry.js with a pinned esbuild, the same recipe geoengine/static/lib/ol uses. entry.js re-exports the WHOLE surface on purpose: JointJS does not tree-shake ({dia, shapes, util} alone measures 431 KB against 462 KB for everything), so a curated entry would buy 7% and add a list to keep in step with its consumers. The artefact also carries @joint/layout-directed-graph 4.3.0 (MPL-2.0, same author) for DAG auto-layout, which pulls @dagrejs/dagre 1.1.8 and @dagrejs/graphlib 2.2.4 (both MIT) with it -- its dependency ranges are ~1.1.4 and ~2.2.4, so neither tracks its own latest (3.1.1 and 4.0.5) and neither should be 'corrected' to it; their licences ship beside this one as LICENSE.dagre and LICENSE.graphlib, and the OSV coordinate above covers @joint/core only. Reached ONLY through a dynamic import() so it never loads on a session that opens no diagram -- the 2.9 MB web_flow charged every session is why that matters. MPL-2.0 combines with this tree's LGPL-3 under MPL section 3.3: no file in the package carries the Exhibit B "Incompatible With Secondary Licenses" notice that would opt out of it.

luxon.notes: Reached only through the @web/core/l10n/luxon facade, never imported directly by feature code. That facade is the seam for an eventual Temporal migration.

odoo_ui_icons.source: IcoMoon build over Carbon + Material icon sets

owl.notes: dist/owl.es.js built (npm ci && npm run build) from Agro-Marin/owl 2.8-marin = odoo/owl v2.8.4 (never published to npm) + four fork commits that let templates be written in owl 3 form ahead of the switch: t-out renders a non-block object as its string (like t-esc and owl 3), a t-call-context template reads its context as `this`, a non-directive attribute on <t t-call> is a value for the callee, and a `.translate` one is a translated literal. __info__.hash names the built commit. Bumping it is a framework-wide change: re-run the full @web suite.

pdfjs.notes: Largest vendored library by far. Sourced from the GitHub prebuilt release zip — the LEGACY one (pdfjs-<v>-legacy-dist.zip), not the modern dist: the modern build calls Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed with no feature detection and never defines it, and that method only reached Baseline in February 2026 (Firefox 144, Safari 26.2, Chrome 145), so PDF preview breaks on every older browser — t24581 was reported from Chrome 141. The legacy build carries the core-js polyfill in both build/pdf.js and build/pdf.worker.js, which a hand-written prototype patch could not do — it would never reach the worker. addons/web/tests/test_pdfjs_dist.py gates the flavour against the bundle files; a runtime check cannot, since a browser that ships the method natively passes it whatever build is vendored. The npm package ships no full viewer. Run through tooling/vendored/mechanise_pdfjs.sh, after which the 12 AgroMarin: markers in web/viewer.js are re-applied. Lazily loaded via @web/core/utils/pdfjs. Since v6 the codecs are separate .wasm files under web/wasm/ — getDocument needs PDFJS_WASM_URL, which the facade defaults.

popper_compat.notes: NOT a vendored library. Self-contained build of @web/libs/popper_compat, which replaced Popper: Bootstrap was its only importer and used a single entry point. Only import-map pages (the IoT box homepage) load this copy; bundles inline the source module instead. Because it derives from in-tree code rather than a pinned release, `rebuild` is run with --check by the drift gate to prove it is not stale.

prismjs.notes: Custom download bundling a fixed language set; re-select the same languages when bumping (see the header comment).

zxing-library.notes: Not a pristine upstream file: a single-file ESM bundle built from the npm package's esm/ sources with ts-custom-error inlined. The build command, including the pinned esbuild version, is in the file's banner. Only ever fetched by browsers without BarcodeDetector.
